thread.title: Dow Leads Stock Market Today To Another Gain; Has It Bottomed?

author: EdJenner
title: Dow Leads Stock Market Today To Another Gain; Has It Bottomed?
text:
Go to Article
The major indexes extended their gains in the stock market today after paring sharp early losses throughout the session. Solid moves by Verizon ( VZ ), Home Depot ( HD ) and Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ) on the Dow offset a big drop by United Technologies ( UTX ).
X
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 0.4%; the S&P 500 climbed 0.3%. Tech stocks weighed on the Nasdaq, which finished flat. Small caps lagged, with the Russell 2000 down 0.9%. Volume was mixed, tracking slightly lower on the NYSE but higher on the Nasdaq vs. Monday.
United Tech gapped down and sank 4% in heavy volume. The stock fell to its lowest point in a month before closing off the session low. The industrial conglomerate, which completed a $23 billion buy of Rockwell Collins, offered details on its breakup into three separate companies . It expects the breakup plan to cost $3 billion.
Meantime, Verizon extended its gains for a second straight session with a 2.5% move. Shares are extended from a 54.87 buy point of a long saucer base. The relative strength line is at a new high, a bullish sign. Among other blue chips, Home Depot added 2% and Walgreens gained 2% to a 14-month high.
Cisco ( CSCO ) and Intel ( INTC ) rose more than 1% each to lead big-cap tech names on the Dow. But Apple ( AAPL ) slid 0.2% for its fifth decline in the past six sessions. Shares are 25% off their peak and 10% below the 200-day moving average. Tuesday’s drop came amid concerns that the U.S. will slap import tariffs on mobile phones and notebook computers made in China. Airlines Soar In Stock Market Today
Airlines, retailers and telecom stocks were among the top sector gainers in the stock market today . Dairy, steel and apparel lagged.
Over in the IBD 50, leaders scoring gains included Nexstar Media Group ( NXST ), UnitedHealth Group ( UNH ) and Medical Properties Trust ( MPW ), up about 2% each.
The biggest IBD 50 losers were Canada Goose ( GOOS ) and Dave & Buster’s Entertainment ( PLAY ), down 5% each, while Five Below ( FIVE ), Wingstop ( WING ) and Horizon Pharma ( HZNP ) shed more than 2% apiece.
